settings.heading: Born from Psalm 23:5
settings.text:
Inspired by Psalm 23:5, “You anoint my head with oil; my cup runneth over,” My Cup Runneth Over was born from a deep love for biblical tradition and the sacred practice of anointing.

Each of our oils is handcrafted with prayer, blending pure natural essences with spiritual intention. Whether you use anointing oil for personal prayer, worship services, or as a meaningful gift, our oils are designed to draw you closer to the divine. We believe the act of anointing is more than a ritual. It is an invitation for God's grace to overflow in your life.

settings.question: What is anointing oil used for?
settings.answer: Anointing oil is a sacred substance used in prayer, worship, and spiritual ceremonies. Rooted in biblical tradition, it is applied to the forehead, hands, or other areas as an act of faith, consecration, and blessing. Christians use anointing oil for personal prayer, healing prayers, anointing the sick (James 5:14), dedicating homes and spaces, ordaining ministers, and as a point of contact for faith during spiritual warfare.

settings.question: How do I use anointing oil for prayer?
settings.answer: Begin by setting an atmosphere of worship. Place a small amount of oil on your fingertip and apply it to your forehead, hands, or the area you wish to anoint while speaking your prayer aloud or silently. You can anoint yourself, pray over loved ones, or dedicate objects and spaces. There is no single “right” way. The oil is a tool of faith that accompanies your sincere prayer to God.

settings.question: What ingredients are in your anointing oils?
settings.answer: Our anointing oils are crafted from 100% natural ingredients. Each blend starts with a base of premium olive oil, the same oil referenced throughout Scripture for anointing. Depending on the blend, we add pure essential oils and natural fragrances such as frankincense, myrrh, spikenard, hyssop, rose, pomegranate, and lily extracts. We never use artificial chemicals, synthetic fillers, or harsh additives. Full ingredient details are listed on each product page.

settings.question: Are your oils safe for skin?
settings.answer: Yes. Our anointing oils are made with gentle, skin-safe natural ingredients and are designed for topical application on the forehead, hands, and wrists. As with any product containing essential oils, do a small patch test on the inside of your wrist before first use, especially if you have sensitive skin or known allergies. If irritation occurs, discontinue use. Our Classic Unscented oil is ideal for those with fragrance sensitivities.

settings.question: What is the shelf life?
settings.answer: Stored in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight, our anointing oils keep for approximately 12 to 18 months. Keep the cap tightly sealed after use to preserve the fragrance and quality of your oil.

settings.question: Can I order for my church or ministry?
settings.answer: Yes. Our 4 oz bottles are well suited to congregational use, and we work with churches and ministries on larger orders. Send us a message through the contact page with what you need and we will reply with options.

settings.title: Anointed at His baptism
settings.verse: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power.
settings.text: At the Jordan the Spirit descended upon Him. Every anointing that followed points back to this one.

settings.title: By the woman who loved much
settings.verse: She began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
settings.text: In a Pharisee's house, a woman with a past poured out her ointment and was forgiven.

settings.title: By Mary of Bethany
settings.verse: Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus.
settings.text: Six days before the Passover, and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.

settings.title: At the house of Simon
settings.verse: She brake the box, and poured it on his head.
settings.text: In Bethany, an alabaster box broken over His head. “She is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying.”

settings.title: For His burial
settings.verse: Nicodemus… brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.
settings.text: Joseph and Nicodemus wound His body in linen with the spices. On the third day, the tomb was empty.

settings.heading: The five anointings of Jesus
settings.text: Five moments in Scripture when Jesus was anointed, and the oil that honors each one.

settings.heading: Eight oils. Eight passages.
settings.text: Every blend carries its verse on the label. 4 oz glass bottles.

settings.label: Cleansing and a fresh start
settings.why: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean.” For confession, renewal and protection.

settings.label: Strength in a hard season
settings.why: The costly spikenard Mary poured at the feet of Jesus. For strength and joy in His presence.

settings.label: Intercession for others
settings.why: The gifts brought to the newborn King. For intercession and prophecies fulfilled.

settings.label: A fresh outpouring of the Spirit
settings.why: “I will give you the rain of your land in his due season.” For obedience rewarded.

settings.label: Abundance and fruitfulness
settings.why: For embracing life, abundance and the fruit of the Spirit.

settings.label: Comfort and God’s love
settings.why: “I am the rose of Sharon.” For the redeemed and the consoled.

settings.label: Peace and trust
settings.why: “Consider the lilies of the field.” For resting in the Father’s love.
